resources.string: When Android hides the channel of the car hotspot, reads it from the firmware\'s hotspot configuration and also tells the iPhone the BSSID of the hotspot. Requires root (Magisk). Applies at the next connection.
Turn the car hotspot on with root (experimental)

When DiPlay opens and before a wireless connection, turns the car\'s saved hotspot on if it is off, with the same steps as over ADB, run through root as the shell user. For firmware whose Android does not let an app start the hotspot. Turn on opening DiPlay after the car starts so the hotspot comes up at every start. Requires root (Magisk). The hotspot is not turned off automatically. Applies at once.
DiPlay could not get root access to turn the hotspot on. Allow root for DiPlay in Magisk or open the hotspot in car settings.
Disconnect iPhone Bluetooth during wireless CarPlay (experimental)

Once wireless CarPlay starts, disconnects the Bluetooth calls, music, contacts and media controls of the iPhone from the head unit, as the car\'s own CarPlay does. For firmware that pauses CarPlay music over Bluetooth. CarPlay keeps running over Wi-Fi; the iPhone does not reconnect Bluetooth by itself afterwards. With several paired iPhones, choose yours in DiPlay: with its Bluetooth disconnected, DiPlay cannot pick it on its own next time. Requires root (Magisk). Applies at the next connection.
Let CarPlay audio through the car firewall (experimental)

While wireless CarPlay runs on the car hotspot, adds a firewall rule that accepts UDP from the iPhone on the hotspot and removes it when the session ends. For firmware whose firewall cuts CarPlay sound after a few seconds. Requires root (Magisk). Applies at the next connection.

The recorder input DiPlay uses for CarPlay calls and Siri. Auto keeps DiPlay\'s own choice. Try another input if the other party or Siri cannot hear you. The voice assistant bus records from the head unit\'s bus14_vr_in input and uses Auto where there is none. All cabin microphones records every channel of the microphone input and mixes them, so passengers in the back are heard too, and uses Auto where the head unit refuses. Applies from the next call or Siri request, without reconnecting.
Show CarPlay music on the dashboard and media widgets (experimental)

Shows the CarPlay track, artist, album and cover in the music widget of the stock instrument cluster and in the music widgets of the driver and passenger screens, and clears them when CarPlay ends. The widget buttons control CarPlay. Uses root (Magisk) only if the head unit refuses DiPlay\'s own request. Applies at once.
CarPlay calls on the dashboard and HUD (experimental)

Shows CarPlay calls in the call widget of the stock instrument cluster and the HUD, and on the custom dashboard. While a call rings, the previous key on the steering wheel declines it and the next key answers; during a call, previous turns the microphone off or on and next hangs up. For firmware where the Bluetooth phone is disconnected during CarPlay; otherwise the dashboard can show a call twice. Applies at once.
Pause CarPlay when the car plays its own audio (experimental)

When the radio or another app of the head unit starts playing, DiPlay pauses the iPhone instead of playing both at once. For firmware whose players take Android audio focus but leave DiPlay\'s audio playing. Start the music in CarPlay again to switch back. Until then the steering-wheel media keys stay with the car\'s source. Applies at once.
Hold next or previous on the steering wheel to fast-forward or rewind (experimental)

While the next or previous key on the steering wheel is held, moves the CarPlay track 10 seconds forward or back every half second. A short press still skips the track. For firmware that tells apps a wheel key is held without skipping the track. Does nothing for live streams and radio, during a CarPlay call, while the car\'s own source or video player has the wheel keys, or with CarPlay audio on the car\'s Bluetooth. Applies at the next connection.

While CarPlay is connected, DiPlay draws its own dashboard on the instrument cluster: the CarPlay map in the middle, with the clock, outside temperature, trip and music around it in place of the side widgets of the stock dashboard. The firmware keeps drawing the speed, warning lights and bottom line over it. For firmware that shows Android\'s cluster display in its engineering mode. Turn off the GMC custom dashboard first. Together with the dashboard map on the centre screen, CarPlay needs one more video decoder. Needs \"Draw over other apps\". Turning it on applies at the next connection; turning it off applies at once.
The card changes at once; the iPhone sends the map in the new size after you reconnect.
Backdrop under the driver assist icon
The firmware draws its driver assistance icon over the dashboard at one place left of the map, and a wide map runs under it. A frosted backdrop sets the icon apart from the map. Applies at once.
While CarPlay guides you, the next turn, its distance and the street are in the map\'s top left corner. Applies at once.
While CarPlay guides you, the arrival time and the minutes and kilometres left are in the map\'s top right corner. Applies at once.
Trip data from the QNX side…
Trip data: off, no QNX password

For firmware that keeps the trip computer on its QNX side. DiPlay logs in to the QNX shell at 192.168.8.1:3333 as root while the dashboard shows and every 5 seconds only reads the trip (distance, driving time, average consumption) from the stock cluster. The password stays on this head unit and is not in settings backups.

With the dashboard in the firmware\'s engineering mode, DiPlay sets the cluster flag that shows the stock RPM, odometer, fuel, coolant, ECO and gear line whenever something else has cleared it, through the QNX login of the trip data. It only writes that one flag while the engineering mode is on, at most five times while the dashboard shows. Needs the QNX password. Applies at once.

While CarPlay guides you along a route, DiPlay draws the next maneuver on the head-up display: the sign with the roundabout exit, the distance and the street, and below them the lanes and the time and distance left. Without a route the head-up display stays empty. For firmware that shows an Android display on the head-up display. If the HUD Renderer app (org.monjaro.hudrenderer) is installed, turn its output off first, or both draw at once. Needs \"Draw over other apps\". Applies at once.
Shows the lanes of the next junction when the iPhone sends them, with the recommended lane underlined.
Time and distance left on the HUD
Shows the time and distance to the destination after the lanes, only when they fit whole.
